title: Compact, review-specific tool payloads instead of 40-field dumps
situation: Long pull requests are causing the review step to run near the context limit. The trace shows each file-analysis tool call appends a large tool result payload with build metadata, ownership data, full lint output, historical CI runs, and dependency details, even though the reviewer uses only a small subset of those fields.
question: What change best addresses the reliability issue?

options.A: Increase max_tokens for the review response and instruct Claude to ignore irrelevant tool result fields.
options.B: Enable context editing to clear old tool results after the request crosses a configured threshold.
options.C: Change the tool wrapper to return compact, review-specific tool result payloads with only the fields needed.
options.D: Apply prompt caching to the tool definitions and repeated review prefix to reduce context window pressure.

why: Tool-heavy review agents often fail because tool results become part of the conversation context. Anthropic documents that tool definitions and accumulated tool_result blocks can exhaust context in long-running agents, and the context window includes messages, tool results, tool definitions, and generated output. Every field returned by a tool is something Claude must carry forward if it remains in messages; a 40-field payload is not harmless just because the prompt says only a few fields matter. The most reliable fix is to shape the tool output before creating the tool result, returning only the review-relevant evidence needed for the next reasoning step. Other mechanisms solve different problems: prompt caching can reduce billing and latency for repeated prefixes, but cached tokens still count toward the context window; context editing can clear older tool results, but it is not a substitute for designing compact current tool outputs. Tool results are returned inside normal user messages rather than a separate tool role. (Docs: manage tool context, context windows, handle tool calls.)
expected_outcome: The verbose analysis payload is tens of kilobytes; the compact one is a few hundred bytes. Shaping the tool result is what keeps a long PR review inside the context window.

rubric.criterion: the compact payload is under 5% of the verbose payload
the compact payload still carries the fields a reviewer uses (changed lines, functions, tests)
learner can say why caching or a bigger max_tokens does not shrink the context the model carries
